job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today our teacher took us to the Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve. I learned that this area is not a zoo, but a protected place where wildlife lives freely in its natural habitat. We saw a special type of wild mango tree that grows only here and nowhere else in the world; our teacher called it an endemic species. I was surprised to learn that plants actually release carbon dioxide during respiration, just like us, though they take in more for photosynthesis. We also discussed how cutting down trees reduces the water cycle, leading to less rainfall because trees release water vapor into the air. My friend Rahul asked if we could just plant any fast-growing trees from other countries to fix the forest. The teacher explained that true reforestation requires planting the same native species that were originally there to restore the ecosystem properly. It made me realize that protecting our environment is much more complex than just planting random seeds or recycling paper. We must preserve the delicate balance of our forests to keep our planet healthy and cool.
response.summary: The passage explains the importance of protecting natural habitats and native plant species. It highlights how deforestation impacts rainfall and clarifies the true meaning of reforestation.
